title: Detecting and handling errors
recap: Error handling has separate jobs: detect an invalid situation, report it to the right layer, and recover or stop deliberately. A reusable calculation generally should not decide how the user interface reports its errors.
Check a dangerous operation before performing it. A sentinel works only when it cannot be confused with a successful value; otherwise use a richer result representation.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement safeRemainder(value, divisor). For value >= 0 and divisor > 0, return value % divisor. Otherwise return -1 without performing remainder. The sentinel is unambiguous because successful remainders are nonnegative. Do not halt the process or print an error.
hints: Do not use % before checking the divisor.
Return the sentinel for invalid inputs and the computed remainder otherwise.
